title: Post-ageing guided closed-loop discovery of multi-element alloy catalysts for automotive exhaust purification

questions.broad: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.
questions.problem_constrained: Starting from a multi-element automotive alloy catalyst containing multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios, what single intervention could overcome activity loss and durability limitations while maintaining low platinum-group-metal consumption during transient and low-temperature gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation, including exposure to H2O and NO and degradation associated with thermal aging or increasing mileage? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the untreated starting catalyst, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.
questions.expert_context: Earlier automotive-catalyst research reported that Cu–Ni catalysts can oxidize CO and hydrocarbons at lower temperatures without platinum-group metals, while Pd–Cu and Pt–Cu catalysts can resist poisoning by H2O and NO and enable oxidation below 150 °C. Multi-principal-element catalysts in nearly equiatomic ratios have also been explored as a framework for combining high activity, thermal stability, and reduced platinum-group-metal use. These prior results demonstrate individual capabilities but do not establish the combined performance demanded by increasingly stringent regulations: clean exhaust during transient and low-temperature operation, resistance to relevant poisons, and durability over a vehicle lifetime despite the mileage-related degradation observed in real-driving-emission studies. Starting from a near-equiatomic, multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst, what single intervention could address this combined activity, poisoning-resistance, and lifetime-durability problem without sacrificing low platinum-group-metal use? State one hypothesis identifying the intervention, explaining how it would work, predicting the change relative to the unmodified catalyst, defining the exhaust and aging conditions over which it should apply, citing supporting prior evidence, and specifying an experiment whose result would falsify it.

gap.evidence: the need for enhanced catalyst durability and regeneration strategies
gap.reason: The introduction motivates improved automotive catalyst materials that maintain high activity under low-temperature and transient conditions, resist degradation over vehicle lifetimes, and reduce platinum-group-metal consumption.
